dongye.t: An early people of Korea's east coast, noted in Chinese records for clan territories, a sky-worship festival and fine bows and small horses.
dongye.o: Dongye occupied the eastern coast of the peninsula, roughly modern Gangwon and southern Hamgyong. After 108 BCE it came under the Han commandery of Lintun, later folded into Lelang, and Chinese sources treat its people as kin of [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] in language and custom.
dongye.r: There was no king; local chiefs ruled, and each clan's hills and rivers were bounded so that trespassers paid fines in slaves or [[e:cattle|cattle]]. Marriage within the clan was forbidden. In the tenth month people held the mucheon festival, dancing in worship of heaven, and they revered the tiger. Dongye was known for its bows of sandalwood, sea-leopard skins and a breed of small horses.
dongye.e: Dongye fell under [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] control during the 2nd to 4th centuries and was fully absorbed by about 400. Its southern areas later passed to [[s:silla|Silla]].

duchy-of-spoleto.t: Powerful Lombard duchy of central Italy whose later dukes, Guy and Lambert, became kings of Italy and emperors in the 9th century.
duchy-of-spoleto.o: [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] warriors under Faroald I took Spoleto in the Umbrian Apennines around 570, cutting the Byzantine route between [[e:rome|Rome]] and [[s:lordship-of-ravenna|Ravenna]]. The duchy grew into a large territory covering much of Umbria, the Marche and Abruzzo, largely independent of the kings in [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]].
duchy-of-spoleto.r: The dukes of Spoleto acted like rulers in their own right, waging war on the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] and sometimes defying the [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] kings; Transamund II was deposed by Liutprand. After 774 it passed to Frankish dukes but kept its weight. Guy of Spoleto was crowned King of [[e:italy|Italy]] in 889 and emperor in 891, and his son Lambert also became emperor. The town's Romanesque churches reflect its medieval wealth.
duchy-of-spoleto.e: In the 10th to 12th centuries the duchy was often held with Camerino or [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]] by imperial appointees. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] sacked Spoleto in 1155. In 1198 [[e:papacy|Pope]] Innocent III took the duchy into the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]], where it remained until 1860.

duchy-of-milan.t: Northern Italy's richest state under the Visconti and Sforza, scene of Leonardo's Last Supper, and later a prize held by Spain and Austria.
duchy-of-milan.o: In 1395 Gian Galeazzo Visconti bought the title of duke from Emperor Wenceslas, turning the [[s:lordship-of-milan|Lordship of Milan]] into an imperial duchy. Gian Galeazzo expanded it far into central [[e:italy|Italy]] before his sudden death in 1402.
duchy-of-milan.r: After the last Visconti, Filippo Maria, died in 1447 and the [[s:golden-ambrosian-republic|Golden Ambrosian Republic]] failed, the condottiere Francesco Sforza became duke in 1450. [[e:milan|Milan]] was a centre of arms making, [[e:silk|silk]] and wool, with a strong bureaucracy. Ludovico Sforza employed Leonardo da Vinci, who painted the Last Supper. [[e:france|France]] invaded in 1499; after the last Sforza died in 1535 [[s:habsburg-spain|Habsburg Spain]] ruled through governors, followed by [[e:austria|Austria]] from 1714, whose reforms suited thinkers such as Cesare Beccaria.
duchy-of-milan.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] army entered [[e:milan|Milan]] in 1796, and the duchy was replaced by the [[s:transpadane-republic|Transpadane Republic]] and then in 1797 the [[s:cisalpine-republic|Cisalpine Republic]]. [[e:austria|Austria]] later ruled [[e:lombardy|Lombardy]] as part of the [[s:kingdom-of-lombardy-venetia|Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia]].

duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.t: The Ascanian duchy on the middle Elbe that won the Saxon electoral vote in 1356 and became the core of the Electorate of Saxony.
duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.o: After the fall of Henry the Lion in 1180, the [[e:saxons|Saxon]] ducal title passed to the Ascanian Bernhard of [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]], whose heirs held lands around Wittenberg on the Elbe and around [[s:duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg|Lauenburg]] in the north. In 1296 the inheritance was partitioned: Albert II kept Wittenberg, while his nephews received the Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg.
duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.r: The duchy was small, but its Ascanian dukes claimed the full dignity of the old [[s:duchy-of-saxony|Duchy of Saxony]], including the office of imperial arch-marshal and a vote in royal elections, which [[s:duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg|Lauenburg]] disputed. Rudolf I was a close ally of [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]]. The territory was agrarian, with Wittenberg a modest residence town at an important Elbe crossing.
duchy-of-saxe-wittenberg.e: The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] settled the dispute in Wittenberg's favour, recognising Rudolf I as prince-elector and creating the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]. When the Ascanian line died out in 1422, the electorate passed to the Wettin margraves of Meissen.

duchy-of-masovia.t: The long-lived duchy of central Poland whose duke invited the Teutonic Knights and whose town of Warsaw became Poland's capital.
duchy-of-masovia.o: Masovia, on the middle Vistula with its centre at [[s:duchy-of-plock|Plock]], was given to Boleslaw IV the Curly under the testament of Boleslaw III in 1138. From 1199 it was held by Konrad I and his descendants, a branch of the Piasts that ruled it for over three centuries.
duchy-of-masovia.r: Exposed to raids by the pagan Prussians and Lithuanians, Konrad I invited the Teutonic Order in 1226 and gave it the land of Chelmno, a decision with lasting consequences. Masovia was a poor, heavily forested land with a large petty nobility. Its dukes often divided it into smaller duchies such as [[s:duchy-of-plock|Plock]] and Rawa, and from 1351 they were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Polish king.
duchy-of-masovia.e: Janusz I made [[e:warsaw|Warsaw]] his main seat in the early 15th century. When the last dukes, Stanislaw and Janusz III, died young in 1524 and 1526, Masovia was incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569), and Warsaw became the royal capital in 1596.

danish-west-indies.t: Denmark's Caribbean sugar colony of St Thomas, St John and St Croix, built on slave labour and sold to the United States in 1917.
danish-west-indies.o: The Danish West [[e:india|India]] Company settled St Thomas in 1672 and St John in 1718, and bought St Croix from [[e:france|France]] in 1733. Charlotte Amalie on St Thomas, with its excellent harbour, became the capital and a busy free port.
danish-west-indies.r: [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] and [[e:cotton|cotton]] plantations worked by enslaved Africans made the islands profitable; at their peak most of the population was enslaved. An uprising on St John in 1733 was crushed with French help. In 1848, facing a revolt on St Croix, Governor-General Peter von Scholten declared emancipation. Charlotte Amalie thrived as a trading and coaling port where English and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] [[e:criollo-people|creole]] were widely spoken.
danish-west-indies.e: After [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] declined, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] sought to sell the islands. During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] the [[s:united-states|United States]], worried about German naval bases, bought them for 25 million dollars, and they were transferred in 1917, becoming the [[s:united-states-virgin-islands|United States Virgin Islands]].

duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.t: The richest of the late medieval Bavarian duchies, ruled from Landshut by the 'Rich Dukes' and famed for the Landshut Wedding of 1475.
duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.o: In 1392 the three sons of Duke Stephen II divided Bavaria: Frederick took Bavaria-Landshut, John II the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-munich|Duchy of Bavaria-Munich]] and Stephen III the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-ingolstadt|Duchy of Bavaria-Ingolstadt]]. Landshut, seat of the Lower Bavarian dukes since the 13th century, became capital of the wealthiest share, which gained part of the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-straubing|Duchy of Bavaria-Straubing]] in 1429 and all of Ingolstadt in 1447.
duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.r: Three successive dukes, Henry XVI, Louis IX and George, were known as the Rich for the treasure they amassed from [[e:silver|silver]], salt tolls and strict financial administration, kept in Trausnitz castle and the fortress of Burghausen. Louis IX founded the University of Ingolstadt in 1472, and the wedding of George to Hedwig Jagiellon in 1475 was among the most lavish festivals of the age.
duchy-of-bavaria-landshut.e: George died in 1503 without sons, leaving his lands to his son-in-law Rupert of the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] in breach of Wittelsbach house law. The War of the Landshut Succession of 1503 to 1505 gave most lands to Albert IV of Bavaria-Munich, while [[s:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]] was created for Rupert's sons.

deciates.t: Ligurian people near Antibes whose attacks on Greek colonies brought the first Roman army into southern Gaul in 154 BCE.
deciates.o: The Deciates were a Ligurian people living in the hills behind Antipolis (Antibes), a colony of [[s:massalia|Massalia]]. Polybius is the main source.
deciates.r: Like other Ligurian peoples of the coast they lived in fortified hilltop settlements and combined farming and herding with raids on the Greek coastal towns.
deciates.e: In 154 BCE the Deciates and the [[s:oxybii|Oxybii]] besieged Antipolis and Nikaia, and [[s:massalia|Massalia]] appealed to the [[s:roman-republic|Roman Republic]]. The consul Quintus Opimius defeated them and handed part of their land to Massalia. Their territory later lay within the Roman province of Gallia Narbonensis.

denmark-norway.t: The Oldenburg kings' twin realm of Denmark and Norway, a Lutheran absolute monarchy with colonies from India to the Caribbean, lasting until 1814.
denmark-norway.o: After [[e:sweden|Sweden]] left the [[s:kalmar-union|Kalmar Union]] in 1523, [[e:denmark|Denmark]] and [[e:norway|Norway]] remained under one king, Frederick I. His son Christian III introduced the Lutheran [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1536 and declared Norway a province of the Danish crown in 1537, though it kept its own laws. The realm also included [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]], the Faroes, Greenland, and the duchies of Schleswig and [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]].
denmark-norway.r: Copenhagen was the centre of government, funded by the Sound Toll on shipping into the Baltic. Christian IV built palaces and towns but lost wars with [[e:sweden|Sweden]], and in 1658 [[e:denmark|Denmark]] ceded [[e:scania|Scania]]. Frederick III introduced absolute monarchy in 1660, set down in the King's Law of 1665. Trading companies founded [[s:danish-india|Danish India]], the [[s:danish-gold-coast|Danish Gold Coast]] and the [[s:danish-west-indies|Danish West Indies]], and Norwegian [[e:timber|timber]] and fish fed a growing merchant fleet.
denmark-norway.e: Allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] after the British bombardment of Copenhagen in 1807, Denmark-[[e:norway|Norway]] ended on the losing side. By the Treaty of [[e:kiel|Kiel]] in 1814 [[e:denmark|Denmark]] ceded Norway to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] but kept [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]], the Faroes and Greenland. Norway briefly declared independence as the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]] (1814) before entering [[s:sweden-norway|Sweden-Norway]].

dhenkanal-state.t: A princely state in central Odisha, remembered for the killing of the twelve-year-old boatman Baji Rout during the Praja Mandal movement of 1938.
dhenkanal-state.o: Tradition holds that Hari Singh Vidyadhar, a commander of the [[s:gajapati-kingdom|Gajapati Kingdom]], defeated a local chief named Dhenka and founded the state in 1529. The capital was the town of Dhenkanal.
dhenkanal-state.r: Dhenkanal was a large inland state on the Brahmani, with [[e:rice|rice]] fields, forest and Adivasi communities. It was tributary to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and from 1803 one of the Orissa Tributary Mahals. In October 1938 state police fired on villagers at Bhuban, and the young ferryman Baji Rout was shot for refusing to take them across the river.
dhenkanal-state.e: Dhenkanal merged into Orissa on 1 January 1948 and is now a district of Odisha.

da-tianxing.t: A one-year dynasty in Yunnan under Zhao Shanzheng, a figurehead raised to the throne at Yangjumie after the fall of Da Changhe.
da-tianxing.o: In 928 the powerful official Yang Ganzhen overthrew [[s:zheng-wang-shichong|Zheng]] Longdan, last ruler of [[s:da-changhe|Da Changhe]], and placed the minister Zhao Shanzheng on the throne at Yangjumie as ruler of Da Tianxing.
da-tianxing.r: Almost nothing is known of the regime beyond its existence; Zhao Shanzheng appears to have been a puppet of Yang Ganzhen and the great families of the Erhai region, who continued the institutions inherited from [[s:nanzhao|Nanzhao]].
da-tianxing.e: In 929 Yang Ganzhen removed Zhao Shanzheng and took the throne himself, founding [[s:da-yining|Da Yining]]. The rapid succession of dynasties ended only with the [[s:dali-kingdom|Dali Kingdom]] in 937.

dutch-cape-colony.t: The Dutch East India Company's colony at the Cape of Good Hope, from which European settlement and the Afrikaans language spread across South Africa.
dutch-cape-colony.o: In 1652 Jan van Riebeeck landed at Table Bay to set up a refreshment station for [[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]] ships sailing to the [[e:east-indies|East Indies]]. From 1657 the Company released servants as free [[e:burghers|burghers]] to farm, and the settlement expanded at the expense of Khoikhoi herders, who were defeated in wars in 1659 and 1673–77.
dutch-cape-colony.r: The colony was run by Company officials, including Simon van der Stel and his son Willem Adriaan, and its economy depended on wine, wheat and enslaved labour brought from the [[e:east-indies|East Indies]], [[e:india|India]] and Madagascar. French Huguenots arrived in 1688. Trekboer [[e:cattle|cattle]] farmers pushed the frontier east to the Fish River, where they met the Xhosa, and Afrikaans developed from Cape [[e:dutch|Dutch]].
dutch-cape-colony.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] seized the Cape in 1795 after the Battle of Muizenberg, returned it to the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]] in 1803 and took it again after the Battle of Blaauwberg in 1806. It became the British [[s:cape-colony|Cape Colony]].

dasada-state.t: A small state of the Jhalawad district of Kathiawar, on the edge of the Little Rann of Kutch, held by a Muslim chiefly family.
dasada-state.o: Dasada lay on the southern edge of the Little Rann of [[s:cutch-state|Kutch]] in the Jhalawad region of northern Kathiawar. Its rulers, a Muslim family of Malik descent, held the estate from around 1600, though its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
dasada-state.r: The ruler governed a dry, thinly settled territory of grazing land and [[e:cotton|cotton]] villages bordering the salt flats. The state paid tribute to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads]] of [[s:baroda-state|Baroda]] and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the Kathiawar Agency. Few further details are recorded.
dasada-state.e: Dasada merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in present Surendranagar district.

duchy-of-western-zhou.t: The tiny duchy around Luoyang that sheltered the last Zhou kings and surrendered to Qin in 256 BCE, ending the Zhou royal line.
duchy-of-western-zhou.o: In 440 BCE King Kao of Zhou enfeoffed his younger brother Jie, Duke Huan, at Henan (the old royal city of Wangcheng, near [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]]). The duchy took over much of what remained of the shrunken royal domain.
duchy-of-western-zhou.r: The dukes of [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] were the real masters of the land around the king, who by the 4th century BCE had almost no territory of his own. After a succession dispute in 367 BCE the domain split, with the [[s:duchy-of-eastern-zhou|Duchy of Eastern Zhou]] ruling around Gong. King Nan lived under the protection of Western Zhou, and the duchy survived by playing off the great powers.
duchy-of-western-zhou.e: In 256 BCE Duke Wu of [[s:western-zhou|Western Zhou]] joined an alliance against the [[s:state-of-qin|State of Qin]]. [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] attacked, the duke surrendered his 36 towns, and King Nan died that year. Qin removed the Nine Tripods, symbols of royal legitimacy, and the Zhou dynasty came to an end.

duchy-of-bavaria-munich.t: The Wittelsbach duchy centred on Munich that outlasted its rival Bavarian branches and reunited the country under Albert IV in 1505.
duchy-of-bavaria-munich.o: The partition of 1392 gave John II the lands around Munich, the smallest share of the Wittelsbach inheritance in Upper Bavaria. His sons Ernest and William III ruled jointly after 1397, and in 1429 they received a share of the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria-straubing|Duchy of Bavaria-Straubing]].
duchy-of-bavaria-munich.r: The dukes ruled from the Alter Hof in Munich, a city grown rich on the [[e:salt-trade|salt trade]]. Duke Ernest had Agnes Bernauer, the commoner wife of his son Albert III, drowned at Straubing in 1435. Albert IV, duke from 1465, built a stronger, more centralised state, and Munich's Frauenkirche was completed under his rule in 1488.
duchy-of-bavaria-munich.e: Albert IV won the War of the Landshut Succession in 1505 and reunited most of Bavaria. His [[e:primogeniture|primogeniture]] decree of 1506 forbade further divisions, so the [[s:duchy-of-bavaria|Duchy of Bavaria]], with Munich as its capital, remained united from then on.

duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.t: Ernestine duchy in Franconia and Thuringia whose ambitious family married into the royal houses of Europe.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.o: John Ernest, seventh son of Ernest the Pious, received Saalfeld in 1680. When the Duchy of Saxe-Coburg died out in 1699, he gained most of Coburg after a long dispute, forming Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.r: The duchy was Lutheran and small, with debts that led to an imperial debt commission in the 18th century. Duke Ernest Frederick and Duke Francis governed modestly; Francis was a collector whose prints formed the Coburg collections. Duke Ernest I was restored after French occupation in 1807. Francis's children married well: Leopold later became King of the Belgians and [[s:colony-of-victoria|Victoria]], Duchess of Kent, was mother of Queen Victoria.
duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld.e: After [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg]] died out, Ernest I gave up Saalfeld and received Gotha in 1826, forming the [[s:duchy-of-saxe-coburg-and-gotha|Duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha]]. Saalfeld went to Saxe-Meiningen, and the family's dynastic rise continued under the new name.

dingan.t: A small successor state of Balhae in the Yalu valley, which resisted the Khitan for half a century and sought alliance with Song China.
dingan.o: After the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]] destroyed [[s:balhae|Balhae]] in 926, groups of Balhae people in the middle Yalu river valley, beyond effective Khitan control, formed their own state. Its beginnings are obscure; it is first recorded in the 930s and 970s, with a royal house sometimes linked to the Yeol family.
dingan.r: Known almost entirely from Chinese and Korean chronicles, Dingan presented itself as heir to [[s:balhae|Balhae]]. In 970 and 981 its king, recorded as O Hyeon-myeong (Wu Xuanming), sent envoys to the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]], proposing joint action against the Khitan, but no help came.
dingan.e: Emperor Shengzong of [[e:liao-dynasty|Liao]] sent a campaign in 985 that destroyed the kingdom by 986. Its people were deported or fled, many to [[s:goryeo|Goryeo]], which absorbed numerous [[s:balhae|Balhae]] refugees in this period.

duchy-of-cleves.t: A lower Rhine duchy, home of Anne of Cleves, whose union with Jülich and Berg and later inheritance by Brandenburg brought Prussia to the Rhine.
duchy-of-cleves.o: The counts of Cleves appear around 1092, with a castle on a hill above the lower [[e:rhine|Rhine]] at Kleve. Their county lay on both banks of the river near the modern [[e:dutch|Dutch]] border. In 1368 it passed to the counts of the Mark, and Adolf I was raised to duke by Emperor Sigismund in 1417.
duchy-of-cleves.r: Cleves was a wealthy trading land on the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], with towns such as Wesel, Emmerich and Kalkar. In 1521 Duke John III united Cleves with Jülich and Berg, forming the [[s:united-duchies-of-julich-cleves-berg|United Duchies]]. His daughter Anne of Cleves married Henry VIII of [[e:england|England]] in 1540. The dukes favoured the humanist middle way of Erasmus.
duchy-of-cleves.e: After the Jülich succession crisis, the Treaty of Xanten in 1614 gave Cleves to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]], giving the Hohenzollerns their first foothold in the west. [[e:france|France]] took the left bank in 1795, and after 1815 the region returned to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]; it is now part of North Rhine-[[e:peace-of-westphalia|Westphalia]].
duchy-of-cleves.re: Catholic Christianity, later mixed Catholic and Protestant

duchy-of-saxe-romhild.t: Short-lived Ernestine duchy in southern Thuringia, one of the seven shares of Ernest the Pious's inheritance.
duchy-of-saxe-romhild.o: Ernest the Pious of Saxe-Gotha died in 1675, and his sons ruled jointly until they divided the lands in 1680. Henry, the fourth son, received Römhild near the Franconian border, establishing the small Duchy of Saxe-Römhild.
duchy-of-saxe-romhild.r: Henry rebuilt Glücksburg Castle in Römhild and spent heavily on his court, leaving debts far greater than the tiny duchy's revenues. The territory was rural, Lutheran and administered by a handful of officials. Little else distinguishes its short history, which is known mainly from the disputes over its inheritance.
duchy-of-saxe-romhild.e: Henry died without children in 1710. His lands were divided among [[s:duchy-of-saxe-gotha|Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg]], Saxe-Meiningen and Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld after a long dispute, and Römhild later passed to Saxe-Meiningen.

duchy-of-bar.t: A Lorraine county raised to a duchy, divided between French and imperial allegiance, and united with the Duchy of Lorraine under René of Anjou's heirs.
duchy-of-bar.o: Bar-le-Duc's castle was built in the 10th century by Duke Frederick of [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Upper Lorraine]]. In 1033 the county passed to his descendant Sophie of Bar, who around 1038 married Louis of Mousson, count of [[s:county-of-montbeliard|Montbéliard]]; their descendants ruled the county of Bar as a separate principality between [[s:county-of-champagne|Champagne]] and [[e:lorraine|Lorraine]].
duchy-of-bar.r: The counts ruled a fertile land along the Meuse and Ornain. After a defeat by Philip IV, the Treaty of Bruges in 1301 made the western part, the Barrois mouvant, a fief of the French crown, while the rest stayed imperial. Robert I became the first duke in 1354. René of [[s:county-of-anjou|Anjou]] inherited Bar in 1430 from his great-uncle, Cardinal Louis of Bar, and through his wife Isabella gained [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]] in 1431.
duchy-of-bar.e: René's grandson René II united Bar and the [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Duchy of Lorraine]] in 1480, and the two shared rulers thereafter. Like [[e:lorraine|Lorraine]], Bar passed to Stanisław Leszczyński in 1737 and was annexed to the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]] on his death in 1766.

duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.t: Albertine Saxon duchy on the Saale whose lavish court employed musicians and gave Bach an honorary title.
duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.o: After Elector John George I of Saxony died in 1656, his son Augustus, already administrator of the [[s:archbishopric-of-magdeburg|Archbishopric of Magdeburg]], received Weissenfels, Querfurt and other lands under his father's will, founding the Duchy of Saxe-Weissenfels. Augustus built the large Neu-Augustusburg palace at Weissenfels.
duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.r: The duchy was Lutheran and depended on the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]] in foreign affairs. Its court was a centre of music and opera: Handel's father was surgeon to the duke, and Johann Sebastian Bach held the honorary title of Kapellmeister of Weissenfels from 1729. Lavish court spending left the state deeply in debt.
duchy-of-saxe-weissenfels.e: Johann Adolf II, the last duke and a [[e:saxons|Saxon]] field marshal, died in 1746, and the duchy reverted to the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]]. Weissenfels passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1815 and is now in Saxony-Anhalt.

dutch-angola.t: The Dutch West India Company's brief occupation of Luanda, which allied with Queen Njinga before Portugal retook the city in 1648.
dutch-angola.o: During the [[e:dutch|Dutch]]–Portuguese war, a [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] fleet under Cornelis Jol captured Luanda in August 1641, aiming to secure enslaved labour for the [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] plantations of [[s:dutch-brazil|Dutch Brazil]]. The Portuguese withdrew inland to [[s:massangano|Massangano]] on the Kwanza.
dutch-angola.r: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] held Luanda and Benguela, strengthened the fort they called Aardenburgh and shipped captives to [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]]. They allied with Njinga Mbande of the [[s:kingdom-of-matamba|Kingdom of Matamba]] and the [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kingdom of Kongo]] against the Portuguese, and their combined forces won victories in the interior, though they failed to destroy the Portuguese garrison at [[s:massangano|Massangano]].
dutch-angola.e: In August 1648 a fleet from [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] under [[e:salvador|Salvador]] Correia de Sa recaptured Luanda, and the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] surrendered. The episode left [[s:portuguese-angola|Portuguese Angola]] restored and Njinga and [[e:kingdom-of-kongo|Kongo]] exposed to Portuguese reprisals.

democratic-republic-of-georgia.t: Georgia's first modern republic, a Menshevik social democracy that won international recognition before the Red Army invaded in 1921.
democratic-republic-of-georgia.o: With the [[s:transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic|Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic]] collapsing, the Georgian National Council declared independence in Tiflis on 26 May 1918. German troops arrived to protect the new state against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], and after [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat British forces took their place until 1920.
democratic-republic-of-georgia.r: Governed by the Social Democratic (Menshevik) party under Noe Zhordania, the republic held democratic elections, carried out land reform, founded Tbilisi State University in 1918 and adopted a constitution in 1921. It fought border wars with [[s:armenia|Armenia]] and faced risings in South Ossetia and [[s:principality-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]]. [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] recognised its independence in the Treaty of [[e:moscow|Moscow]] of May 1920.
democratic-republic-of-georgia.e: In February 1921 the Red Army invaded, and Tiflis fell on 25 February; the government went into exile in [[e:france|France]]. The [[s:georgian-ssr|Georgian SSR]] replaced it, and independent [[s:georgia|Georgia]] restored its flag in 1990-1991.

don-republic.t: The anti-Bolshevik state of the Don Cossacks in the Russian Civil War, led by Ataman Krasnov and later part of Denikin's White movement.
don-republic.o: After Ataman Alexey Kaledin shot himself in February 1918 as Bolsheviks overran the Don, a [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] uprising in spring drove them out. In May 1918 a Cossack assembly in Novocherkassk elected General Pyotr Krasnov ataman and proclaimed the independent Almighty Don Host, heir to the [[s:don-cossack-host|Don Cossack Host]].
don-republic.r: Krasnov allied with [[e:germany|Germany]], from which he obtained weapons, and organised a sizeable Don army that besieged Tsaritsyn in 1918. The republic had a constitution, its own currency and a government based on [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] institutions. After Germany's defeat Krasnov resigned in February 1919, and under Ataman Afrikan Bogaevsky the Don joined Denikin's Armed Forces of South [[e:russia|Russia]].
don-republic.e: The White advance on [[e:moscow|Moscow]] failed in 1919. The Red Army captured Novocherkassk in January 1920, and the Don was absorbed into the [[s:russian-sfsr|Russian SFSR]]. The Bolsheviks' policy of decossackisation brought executions and [[e:deportation|deportations]].

deceangli.t: People of north-east Wales, the first target of Roman campaigns into Wales in 48, whose lead mines soon stamped their name on Roman ingots.
deceangli.o: The Deceangli lived in what is now Flintshire and Denbighshire, between the Dee estuary and the Clwyd valley, a region of hillforts such as Moel Hiraddug and Penycloddiau. They were probably a small Iron Age grouping of local communities and are first named by [[e:tacitus|Tacitus]].
deceangli.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or society beyond the archaeology of their hillforts and farms. Their territory was rich in lead and [[e:silver|silver]] ores on Halkyn Mountain, which the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] quickly exploited; lead pigs found near Chester carry the inscription DECEANGL and a date of 74, showing that mining was organised under the name of the people.
deceangli.e: In 48 the governor Ostorius Scapula marched against the Deceangli, ravaging their land almost to the Irish Sea before trouble among the [[s:brigantes|Brigantes]] recalled him. The area was secured by the fortress of Chester in the 70s, and the Deceangli are not known to have formed a civitas of [[s:roman-britain|Roman Britain]].

duchy-of-raciborz.t: Upper Silesian duchy on the upper Oder, ruled first by Piasts and then by a Přemyslid branch from Opava until 1521.
duchy-of-raciborz.o: In the 1281 partition of the [[s:duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz|Duchy of Opole and Racibórz]], Przemysław received Racibórz, the old capital of Upper [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]]. His son Leszek accepted Bohemian overlordship in 1327, and when Leszek died without heirs in 1336, the duchy passed to [[e:nicholas-ii|Nicholas II]] of Opava, a Přemyslid married to Przemysław's daughter.
duchy-of-raciborz.r: The Opava Přemyslids ruled Racibórz as part of a combined duchy of Opava and Racibórz, later separate. The duchy was a fertile land of grain and fish ponds, with a Polish-speaking population and German [[e:burghers|burghers]]. It was a Bohemian fief, and its dukes took part in the Hussite wars and the struggles between Bohemian and Hungarian kings.
duchy-of-raciborz.e: After the last Přemyslid duke died in 1521, Racibórz passed to John II the Good of Opole. When he died in 1532, it fell to the Bohemian crown, held by the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and pledged to Brandenburg-Ansbach. It passed to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742 and to [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

dominican-republic.t: The present Dominican Republic since 1966, which moved from the authoritarian rule of Joaquín Balaguer to democracy and fast tourism-led growth.
dominican-republic.o: After the civil war and US intervention of 1965 ended the [[s:third-dominican-republic|Third Dominican Republic]], an interim government organised elections in June 1966. Joaquín Balaguer, a former aide of Trujillo, defeated Juan Bosch and introduced a new constitution in November 1966.
dominican-republic.r: Balaguer ruled for twelve years with repression of the left, public works and [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] exports. The 1978 election brought a peaceful transfer to Antonio Guzmán, but Balaguer returned from 1986 to 1996. Leonel Fernández and Danilo [[e:medina|Medina]] of the Dominican Liberation Party then governed for most of the next two decades. Tourism, free trade zones, mining and remittances from Dominicans in the [[s:united-states|United States]] transformed the economy, making it one of the fastest growing in [[e:latin-america|Latin America]].
dominican-republic.e: Luis Abinader of the Modern Revolutionary Party won the presidency in 2020 and was re-elected in 2024. Relations with neighbouring [[s:republic-of-haiti|Haiti]], migration and inequality remain the central issues of the republic.

dutch-tobago.t: Contested Dutch colony on Tobago, named New Walcheren by Zeeland settlers and fought over by the Dutch, Courlanders, English and French.
dutch-tobago.o: Merchants from [[s:county-of-zeeland|Zeeland]], chiefly the Lampsins brothers of Vlissingen, sent settlers to Tobago in 1628 under a patent from the [[e:dutch-west-india-company|Dutch West India Company]] and called the island New Walcheren. The first colony was destroyed by the Spanish and Kalinago from Trinidad in 1637, but the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] returned in the 1650s, displacing the rival colony of the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland]].
dutch-tobago.r: The colony centred on Lampsinsburg and a cluster of forts and plantations growing tobacco, [[e:cotton|cotton]], [[e:indigo|indigo]] and [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] with the labour of enslaved Africans. In 1662 [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] made Cornelis Lampsins Baron of Tobago, a rare French title over a Dutch-run island. The settlers were mostly [[e:dutch|Dutch]] Reformed Protestants, with French, Jewish and other incomers.
dutch-tobago.e: Tobago changed hands repeatedly during the Anglo-[[e:dutch|Dutch]] and Franco-Dutch wars. In 1677 a French fleet under Jean d'Estrées attacked, and a magazine explosion destroyed the Dutch fort and its defenders. The French razed the colony, and Dutch rule ended; the island stayed thinly settled until the British [[s:colony-of-tobago|Colony of Tobago]] of 1763.

dominion-of-newfoundland.t: Britain's oldest colony, a self-governing dominion from 1907 that gave up self-government during the Depression and joined Canada in 1949.
dominion-of-newfoundland.o: The [[s:colony-of-newfoundland|Colony of Newfoundland]], self-governing since 1855, had declined to join [[s:canada|Canada]] in 1869. At the Imperial Conference of 1907 it was granted the status of a dominion, equal in title to [[e:canada|Canada]], [[s:commonwealth-of-australia|Australia]] and [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]], under Prime Minister Robert Bond, who had sought a separate trade deal with the [[s:united-states|United States]].
dominion-of-newfoundland.r: The economy depended on the salt cod fishery, with newer pulp, paper and iron mining. In the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] the [[e:newfoundland|Newfoundland]] Regiment was almost destroyed at Beaumont-Hamel on 1 July 1916, and war debt, including a costly railway, weighed on the dominion. In 1927 the Privy Council awarded it the interior of Labrador. The Depression brought near-bankruptcy and riots against Prime Minister Richard Squires in 1932.
dominion-of-newfoundland.e: In 1934 [[e:newfoundland|Newfoundland]] gave up self-government to a British-appointed Commission of Government. American and Canadian bases brought prosperity in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]]. After two referendums in 1948, led by Joey Smallwood's campaign, it joined [[s:canada|Canada]] as its tenth province on 31 March 1949.

dar-masalit.t: A sultanate of the Masalit people in western Darfur that defeated a French column in 1910 and joined Sudan by agreement in 1922.
dar-masalit.o: The Masalit lived on the western fringe of the [[s:darfur-sultanate|Darfur Sultanate]]. In the 1870s, as [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]] fell to [[s:zubayrs-bahr-al-ghazal|Zubayr's Bahr al-Ghazal]] and the [[s:khedivate-of-egypt|Khedivate of Egypt]], a Masalit holy man, Ismail Abd al-Nabi, built up authority among them, and his family founded an independent sultanate around 1874.
dar-masalit.r: The sultans ruled a farming people from fortified centres, balancing between the [[s:mahdist-state|Mahdist State]], the [[s:wadai-empire|Wadai Empire]] and the restored [[s:darfur-sultanate|Darfur Sultanate]] of [[e:ali-dinar|Ali Dinar]]. In 1910 [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Taj al-Din defeated a French column at Dorothe, though he died in the fighting. His successor Muhammad Bahr al-Din, known as Andoka, made Geneina his capital.
dar-masalit.e: After [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed [[e:darfur-sultanate|Darfur]] in 1916 and the Anglo-French border was fixed in 1919, the sultan accepted [[e:indirect-rule|indirect rule]]. Dar Masalit was formally joined to [[s:anglo-egyptian-sudan|Anglo-Egyptian Sudan]] in 1922, keeping its sultan as a traditional ruler.

duchy-of-krakow.t: The senior duchy of fragmented Poland, whose throne at Krakow carried overlordship of the other Piast dukes.
duchy-of-krakow.o: In his testament of 1138 Boleslaw III Wrymouth divided [[e:poland|Poland]] among his sons, creating a senior province around Krakow to be held by the eldest Piast with authority over the others. The first senior duke, Wladyslaw II the Exile, tried to rule alone and was driven out by his brothers in 1146.
duchy-of-krakow.r: Krakow passed in turn to Boleslaw IV, Mieszko III and Casimir II the Just, and the seniority principle broke down as rival dukes fought for the city. Lesser [[e:poland|Poland's]] nobles and [[e:bishop|bishops]] gained great influence. The [[e:mongols|Mongols]] devastated the duchy in 1241, but under Boleslaw V the Chaste Krakow received town rights in 1257 and the salt mines of Wieliczka and Bochnia brought wealth.
duchy-of-krakow.e: After the Silesian Henry IV Probus and the Bohemian king Wenceslaus II, who ruled from 1291, Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high took Krakow in 1306. He was crowned there in 1320, and the duchy became the core of the reunited [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1025-1385|Kingdom of Poland]] (1025-1385).

duchy-of-bouillon.t: The Ardennes duchy whose castle Godfrey of Bouillon pawned for the First Crusade, later a small sovereign state of the La Marck and La Tour d'Auvergne families.
duchy-of-bouillon.o: Godfrey of Bouillon pledged his castle and lands to the [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]] in 1096 to fund the [[e:first-crusade|First Crusade]], and the bishops held Bouillon for centuries. From the mid-15th century the La Marck family gained control of it, and by the 1480s they ruled it in practice as an independent duchy.
duchy-of-bouillon.r: Bouillon was a forested, sparsely populated land around a great castle on the Semois. Robert II de la Marck and his heirs, also princes of [[s:principality-of-sedan|Sedan]], styled themselves dukes. Possession was contested between the La Marcks, their La Tour d'[[s:county-of-auvergne|Auvergne]] heirs and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]]. In 1678 [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV]] took Bouillon and gave it to Godefroy-Maurice de La Tour d'Auvergne under French protection.
duchy-of-bouillon.e: French troops annexed the duchy in 1795. After the Napoleonic Wars it went to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-luxembourg|Grand Duchy of Luxembourg]] in 1815 and to the [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Kingdom of Belgium]] in 1839.

dutch-delagoa-bay.t: A short-lived Dutch East India Company trading post on Delagoa Bay, founded to seek gold and ivory and abandoned after a decade.
dutch-delagoa-bay.o: In 1721 the [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] ([[e:dutch-east-india-company|VOC]]) sent an expedition from the Cape to Delagoa Bay, hoping to tap the gold of the interior and the [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] of the bay. The settlers built Fort Lijdzaamheid on the site of modern Maputo.
dutch-delagoa-bay.r: The post traded cloth, [[e:bead|beads]] and metal for [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves with the local Tsonga rulers, including those of the [[s:tembe-kingdom|Tembe Kingdom]]. It suffered terribly from malaria, losing much of its garrison, and was attacked and briefly captured by [[e:piracy|pirates]] in 1722. Expeditions inland failed to find the hoped-for goldfields.
dutch-delagoa-bay.e: Unprofitable and deadly, the post was abandoned in 1730. The Portuguese reasserted their claim to the bay, which was later contested by [[e:austria|Austria]] and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] before the 1875 arbitration confirmed Portuguese possession.

dewas-senior.t: The senior of the two Maratha Puar states that shared the town of Dewas in Malwa, remembered through E. M. Forster's The Hill of Devi.
dewas-senior.o: The brothers Tukoji Rao and Jivaji Rao Puar came to [[e:malwa|Malwa]] with the [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]] [[e:baji-rao-i|Baji Rao I]] and received Dewas around 1728. Their shared holding developed into two states, the Senior Branch descending from Tukoji Rao and the Junior from Jivaji Rao, which divided land and revenues but kept the same capital.
dewas-senior.r: Dewas Senior was a [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] state of the Central [[e:india|India]] Agency, centred on the hill shrine of the goddess Chamunda above the town. Each branch had its own palace, administration and quarter of Dewas. E. M. Forster served as secretary to Maharaja Tukoji Rao III in 1921, an experience he described in The Hill of Devi.
dewas-senior.e: After accession to [[e:india|India]], Dewas Senior merged into [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948, which became part of Madhya Pradesh in 1956.

duchy-of-pomerelia.t: The duchy of Gdansk Pomerania under the Samborides, whose end in 1294 led to centuries of conflict between Poland and the Teutonic Knights.
duchy-of-pomerelia.o: Eastern [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Pomerania]], around Gdansk on the Vistula delta, was conquered by Boleslaw III of [[e:poland|Poland]] in the early 12th century and governed for him by local nobles. In the mid 12th century these governors, the Samborides, began to rule on their own account, and Sambor I founded the Cistercian abbey of Oliwa in 1186.
duchy-of-pomerelia.r: Pomerelia controlled the mouth of the Vistula, and Gdansk grew into a busy port with German, Slavic and Danish merchants. Swietopelk II the Great, who ruled from the 1220s to 1266, threw off Polish overlordship, took the ducal title and fought long wars against the Teutonic Order.
duchy-of-pomerelia.e: His son Mestwin II, who died without sons, left the duchy to Przemysl II of [[s:duchy-of-greater-poland|Greater Poland]] under the Treaty of Kepno of 1282. After Mestwin's death in 1294, the land was contested, and in 1308 the Teutonic Knights seized Gdansk and held Pomerelia until it became part of [[s:royal-prussia|Royal Prussia]] in 1466.

duchy-of-opole.t: Upper Silesian Piast duchy whose duke Władysław Opolczyk brought the Black Madonna to Częstochowa and whose last prince died in 1532.
duchy-of-opole.o: In 1281 the [[s:duchy-of-opole-and-raciborz|Duchy of Opole and Racibórz]] was divided among the sons of Władysław of Opole, and Bolko I received Opole on the Oder. He accepted Bohemian overlordship in 1327 along with other Upper Silesian dukes, while his descendants continued to rule.
duchy-of-opole.r: Władysław II of Opole served as palatine of [[e:hungary|Hungary]] and in 1382 founded the Pauline monastery of Jasna Góra at Częstochowa, bringing the Black Madonna icon. The Opole dukes later gathered much of Upper [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], and John II the Good issued a charter of privileges for the region and allowed the mining town of Tarnowskie Góry to develop. The population was largely Polish-speaking.
duchy-of-opole.e: With John II's death in 1532 the Upper Silesian Piasts died out, and Opole passed to the Bohemian crown under the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]], pledged at times to [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] and the Polish Vasas. It went to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1742 and to [[e:poland|Poland]] in 1945.

dumnonii.t: Iron Age people of Devon and Cornwall, whose tin and remote farming settlements kept them apart from the coin-using kingdoms of the south-east.
dumnonii.o: The Dumnonii emerged from the Iron Age communities of the south-western peninsula, a land of hillforts, defended farmsteads known as rounds, and coastal promontory forts. Greek writers from Pytheas onwards describe the [[e:tin|tin]] trade of the far south-west, and harbours such as Mount Batten on Plymouth Sound linked the region with [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]] and the wider Atlantic world.
dumnonii.r: No kings or coins of the Dumnonii are known, which suggests a looser society of local lineages rather than a single dynasty. Most people lived in small enclosed farms raising [[e:cattle|cattle]] and grain, while [[e:tin|tin]] streaming in Cornwall and Dartmoor gave the region its main export. Courtyard houses and underground passages called fogous are distinctive of the far west.
dumnonii.e: Roman forces reached the south-west after 43, and around 55 the legio II Augusta built a fortress at Exeter. When the army moved on, the town became Isca Dumnoniorum, capital of a self-governing civitas, though the countryside stayed little Romanised. The name survived in the post-[[s:roman-kingdom|Roman Kingdom]] of [[s:kingdom-of-dumnonia|Dumnonia]] and in the county name Devon.

dominion-of-india.t: Independent India's first constitutional form, a Commonwealth dominion that integrated the princely states and drafted the constitution of the republic.
dominion-of-india.o: Under the Indian Independence Act of 1947, the [[s:british-raj|British Raj]] was partitioned, and on 15 August 1947 the [[e:dominion|Dominion]] of [[e:india|India]] was created with Jawaharlal Nehru as prime minister. Lord Mountbatten stayed on as Governor-General until 1948, succeeded by C. Rajagopalachari, the only Indian to hold the post.
dominion-of-india.r: The dominion confronted partition violence and refugee resettlement, and fought the first war with the [[s:dominion-of-pakistan|Dominion of Pakistan]] over [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]]. Vallabhbhai Patel and V. P. Menon integrated more than five hundred [[e:princely-state|princely states]], using force against Hyderabad in 1948. [[e:mahatma-gandhi|Mahatma Gandhi]] was assassinated in January 1948. A Constituent Assembly chaired in drafting by B. R. Ambedkar wrote the new constitution.
dominion-of-india.e: The Constitution of [[e:india|India]] came into force on 26 January 1950, making India a sovereign republic within the Commonwealth and ending the British monarch's role as head of state. The dominion was succeeded by the [[s:republic-of-india|Republic of India]].

dali-kingdom.t: The Buddhist kingdom of the Duan family in Yunnan, which ruled the south-west for over three centuries until the Mongol conquest of 1253.
dali-kingdom.o: In 937 Duan Siping, a commander of Bai descent from the Tonghai region, overthrew [[s:da-yining|Da Yining]] with the help of tribal allies from eastern Yunnan and founded the Dali Kingdom, with its capital at Yangjumie near Lake Erhai.
dali-kingdom.r: Dali was a devoutly Buddhist state; esoteric Acharya [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] was strong, and many kings abdicated to become monks. From the late 11th century the [[e:gao|Gao]] family held hereditary office as chief ministers, and Gao Shengtai briefly took the throne in 1094 before the Duan were restored in 1096. Dali sold horses to the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]] and dominated routes to [[s:myanmar|Burma]].
dali-kingdom.e: In 1253 a Mongol army under Kublai took the capital, and the last king, Duan Xingzhi, submitted. The Duan family continued as hereditary governors under the [[s:yuan-dynasty|Yuan Dynasty]] until the [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]] conquered Yunnan in 1382.

dutch-east-india-company-territories.t: The Asian empire of the Dutch East India Company, a trading firm that ruled ports and provinces from Batavia and controlled the world spice trade.
dutch-east-india-company-territories.o: The [[e:dutch-east-india-company|Dutch East India Company]] (VOC), chartered in 1602, appointed its first Governor-General, Pieter Both, in 1610. In 1619 [[e:jan-pieterszoon-coen|Jan Pieterszoon Coen]] seized Jayakarta and founded [[e:batavia|Batavia]] as its headquarters. The Company then conquered the [[e:banda-islands|Banda Islands]] in 1621, took [[e:malacca|Malacca]] from the Portuguese in 1641 and forced [[s:gowa-sultanate|Makassar]] into the Treaty of Bongaya in 1667.
dutch-east-india-company-territories.r: [[e:batavia|Batavia]] was governed by the Governor-General and the [[e:council-of-the-indies|Council of the Indies]], answering to the [[e:heeren-xvii|Heeren XVII]] in [[e:amsterdam|Amsterdam]]. The Company enforced monopolies on [[e:nutmeg|nutmeg]], [[e:cloves|cloves]] and [[e:pepper|pepper]], used slave labour and forced deliveries, and intervened in the succession wars of the [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram Sultanate]], gaining much of [[e:java|Java]]. Batavia was a multi-ethnic city where Chinese settlers were massacred in 1740.
dutch-east-india-company-territories.e: Corruption, war and falling profits left the Company deeply indebted. It was nationalised by the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]] in 1796 and its charter expired on 31 December 1799, when its possessions passed to the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] state and became the [[s:dutch-east-indies|Dutch East Indies]].

dutch-malacca.t: Dutch-ruled Malacca, taken from Portugal in 1641, which guarded the Strait of Malacca for the Dutch East India Company for nearly two centuries.
dutch-malacca.o: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]], allied with the [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor Sultanate]], besieged [[s:portuguese-malacca|Portuguese Malacca]] for five months and captured it in January 1641. The Company wanted to secure the strait and divert trade to [[e:batavia|Batavia]] rather than revive [[e:malacca|Malacca]] as a great emporium, so the port was ruled as a fortified outpost.
dutch-malacca.r: A governor and council ran the city from the Stadthuys, completed around 1660. [[e:malacca|Malacca]] checked shipping in the strait, bought [[e:tin|tin]] from [[s:perak-sultanate|Perak]] and other Malay states, and sold Indian cloth. Its population mixed [[e:dutch|Dutch]] officials, Portuguese Eurasians, Chinese, Malays and Indians. Jan van Riebeeck, founder of Cape Town, governed it from 1662 to 1665.
dutch-malacca.e: British forces occupied [[e:malacca|Malacca]] in 1795 during the [[e:french-revolutionary-wars|French Revolutionary Wars]] and returned it in 1818. The [[e:anglo-dutch-treaty-of-1824|Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824]] exchanged it for [[s:bencoolen|Bencoolen]], and after the handover in 1825 it became part of the [[s:straits-settlements|Straits Settlements]]. [[e:dutch|Dutch]] buildings still dominate its historic centre.

duchy-of-sorrento.t: Minor Byzantine-era duchy on the Sorrento peninsula, independent of Naples from the 9th century until the Normans took it in 1137.
duchy-of-sorrento.o: Sorrento, an old Roman town on the peninsula south of the Bay of Naples, was part of the Byzantine [[s:duchy-of-naples|Duchy of Naples]]. In the 9th century, amid the conflicts with [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] Benevento and Arab raiders, it gained self-government under its own dukes, like neighbouring [[s:republic-of-amalfi|Amalfi]].
duchy-of-sorrento.r: Little is known of the duchy, which was small and overshadowed by Naples and [[s:republic-of-amalfi|Amalfi]]. It ruled the western part of the peninsula and nearby islands, and its economy rested on fishing, farming and coastal trade. In 1039 Guaimar IV of [[s:principality-of-salerno|Salerno]] seized it and gave it to his brother Guy, and it later passed among [[e:kingdom-of-the-lombards|Lombard]] and Norman lords.
duchy-of-sorrento.e: Sorrento submitted to Roger II and was absorbed into the Norman [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]] by 1137, after which it was ruled as part of the kingdom's mainland territories.

duchy-of-rawa.t: A Masovian duchy in central Poland, one of the last Piast lands, incorporated into the Polish Crown in 1462.
duchy-of-rawa.o: After Boleslaw II of Masovia died in 1313, his lands were divided among his sons, and Siemowit II received the southern part around Rawa. Over the next 150 years Rawa was repeatedly joined to and separated from the other Masovian duchies as the family's branches divided their inheritance.
duchy-of-rawa.r: Rawa was a modest farming land with a brick castle built under Casimir III's influence in the 14th century. Its dukes were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Polish Crown from 1351. Siemowit III reunited most of Masovia in the 1370s and issued laws for it, but it was divided again among his heirs, and Rawa was ruled by the Siemowit and Wladyslaw lines of [[s:duchy-of-plock|Plock]].
duchy-of-rawa.e: When Siemowit VI and Wladyslaw II, the last dukes of the line, died in 1462, King Casimir IV took Rawa and Gostynin into the [[s:kingdom-of-poland-1385-1569|Kingdom of Poland]] (1385-1569). The land became the Rawa Voivodeship.

duchy-of-anhalt.t: Duchy that reunited the Anhalt lands in 1863 and became an industrial region on the Elbe and Saale.
duchy-of-anhalt.o: After the extinction of [[s:principality-of-anhalt-kothen|Anhalt-Köthen]] in 1847 and [[s:principality-of-anhalt-bernburg|Anhalt-Bernburg]] in 1863, Duke Leopold IV Frederick of [[s:principality-of-anhalt-dessau|Anhalt-Dessau]] ruled all the [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]] territories. In 1863 they were formally combined as the Duchy of Anhalt, with Dessau as capital.
duchy-of-anhalt.r: [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]] was small but economically active, with [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] beet, lignite, potash and salt, and later chemical and engineering works. Hugo Junkers founded his first works at Dessau in 1895, later the base of the Junkers aircraft factory. A constitution of 1859, extended to the whole duchy, provided a diet. Anhalt joined the [[s:north-german-confederation|North German Confederation]] in 1867 and the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871.
duchy-of-anhalt.e: Duke Joachim Ernst, a minor, abdicated through his regent in November 1918, and the duchy became the [[s:free-state-of-anhalt|Free State of Anhalt]]. After 1945 its territory was merged into Saxony-Anhalt, which still takes its name in part from the old duchy.

dikwa-emirate.t: A Kanuri emirate south of Lake Chad, carved out of the old Bornu lands that fell to German Kamerun, which joined Nigeria after the 1961 plebiscite.
dikwa-emirate.o: Dikwa had been the capital of [[s:rabih-az-zubayrs-state|Rabih az-Zubayr]], the Sudanese warlord who conquered [[e:bornu|Bornu]] in 1893. After the French killed Rabih in 1900, the European powers restored the al-Kanemi dynasty, but the old lands of the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]] were split by the borders of [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]], [[s:kamerun|Kamerun]] and [[e:chad|Chad]]. The part around Dikwa fell to [[e:germany|Germany]], where a separate shehu was installed.
dikwa-emirate.r: The [[e:emirate|emirate]] kept the Kanuri institutions of [[e:bornu|Bornu]]: a shehu with titled officials, district heads and Islamic courts. Under the Germans, and after 1916 under British rule in the Northern [[e:cameroon|Cameroons]], it was administered through the shehu, with little development. Most people were Kanuri, Shuwa Arab and other farmers and herders.
dikwa-emirate.e: In the 1961 plebiscite the Northern [[e:cameroon|Cameroons]] voted to join [[e:nigeria|Nigeria]], and Dikwa became part of Nigeria's Northern Region, joining its Kanuri kin in the [[s:borno-emirate|Borno Emirate]]. The [[e:emirate|emirate]] survives as a traditional institution in Borno State.

danishmendids.t: A Turkish dynasty of central and north-eastern Anatolia that rivalled the Seljuks of Rum and inspired the epic of Danishmend Gazi.
danishmendids.o: After the Seljuk victory at [[e:battle-of-manzikert|Manzikert]] in 1071, a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] leader known as Danishmend Gazi, whose origins are obscure, conquered Sivas, Tokat, Niksar, Amasya and later [[s:melid|Malatya]], founding one of the first Turkish principalities in [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].
danishmendids.r: The Danishmendids ruled a largely Christian population of [[e:greeks|Greeks]] and [[e:armenians|Armenians]] through [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] warriors and a growing urban Muslim elite. In 1100 Danishmend Gazi captured Bohemond of [[s:principality-of-antioch|Antioch]], and his son Gazi Gumushtigin was for a time the strongest ruler in [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], receiving the title malik from the [[e:caliphate|caliph]]. They built mosques and [[e:madrasa|madrasas]] in Tokat, Niksar and Kayseri. Their deeds were later celebrated in the Danishmendname, a Turkish epic of holy war.
danishmendids.e: After the death of Yagibasan in 1164 the family split and weakened. Kilij Arslan II of the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]] annexed Sivas around 1174 and the [[s:melid|Malatya]] branch in 1178, ending the dynasty.

duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.t: The Farnese duchy in Emilia, later held by Bourbons and by Napoleon's widow Marie Louise, which lasted until Italian unification.
duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.o: In 1545 [[e:papacy|Pope]] Paul III detached [[s:commune-of-parma|Parma]] and [[s:commune-of-piacenza|Piacenza]] from the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]] and gave them to his son Pier Luigi Farnese, already Duke of [[s:duchy-of-castro|Castro]]. Pier Luigi was murdered in 1547 by nobles backed by the imperial governor of [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]].
duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.r: The Farnese built a court at [[s:commune-of-parma|Parma]], with the Pilotta palace and the wooden Teatro Farnese of 1618. Alessandro Farnese, [[e:spain|Spain's]] general in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]], was its most famous duke. When the Farnese died out in 1731, Elisabeth Farnese, queen of Spain, passed the duchy to her son Charles of [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]]. After Austrian rule from 1735, Philip of [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbon]] founded the Bourbon-Parma line in 1748, with reforming minister Guillaume du Tillot.
duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza.e: [[e:france|France]] annexed the duchy in 1802. In 1814 it went to Marie Louise, [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] widow, who ruled until 1847, then back to the [[e:house-of-bourbon|Bourbons]]. In 1859 it joined the [[s:united-provinces-of-central-italy|United Provinces of Central Italy]] and was annexed to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] in 1860.

duchy-of-bytom.t: Upper Silesian Piast duchy whose first duke became the first Silesian prince to pay homage to the King of Bohemia, in 1289.
duchy-of-bytom.o: When Władysław of Opole died in 1281, his lands were divided among his sons. Casimir received Bytom, an old market town in eastern Upper [[s:duchy-of-silesia|Silesia]], together with lands around Gliwice and Koźle. In 1289 he paid homage to Wenceslaus II of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], the first Silesian duke to accept Bohemian overlordship.
duchy-of-bytom.r: The duchy was small, with farmland, forests and early [[e:silver|silver]] and lead mining around Bytom. Casimir's son Władysław ruled it in the early 14th century, and later dukes divided it into smaller shares. The population was largely Polish-speaking, with German settlers in the towns.
duchy-of-bytom.e: After the Bytom line died out in 1355, the duchy was divided between the dukes of Oleśnica and Cieszyn and later fragmented further, with parts passing among Silesian princes until the end of the 15th century. It eventually came under the Bohemian crown, and Bytom is now in [[e:poland|Poland]].

duchy-of-styria.t: Alpine duchy of Graz and the Erzberg iron mountain, a Habsburg land for over six centuries and the shield of Inner Austria against the Ottomans.
duchy-of-styria.o: The March of Styria grew from a Carolingian border zone ruled from the 11th century by the Otakar counts of Steyr. In 1180 Emperor [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] raised it to a duchy for Ottokar IV. By the Georgenberg Pact of 1186 it passed to the Babenbergs of the [[s:duchy-of-austria|Duchy of Austria]] in 1192, and after Ottokar II of [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] it came to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] in 1282.
duchy-of-styria.r: Styria was governed by its dukes with strong estates meeting in the Landhaus at Graz. Iron from the Erzberg made it an industrial heartland. From 1564 Graz was capital of [[s:inner-austria|Inner Austria]] under Archduke Charles II, who invited the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]]; his son Ferdinand II expelled Protestants. Repeated Ottoman raids made defence a constant concern. German was spoken in the north and Slovene in Lower Styria.
duchy-of-styria.e: Styria remained a crown land of the [[s:habsburg-monarchy|Habsburg Monarchy]] and [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]] until 1918. It was then divided: Lower Styria with Maribor went to the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes]] and is now in Slovenia, while the rest became the Austrian state of Styria.
